Start by finding the sum of the first k elements.
When the window moves one position, add the new element and remove the old first element.

title: Largest Average Subarray I

notes: Answers are accepted when the absolute error is less than 10^-5.
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: The window [12, -5, -6, 50] has sum 51, so its average is 51 / 4 = 12.75, which is the maximum.
There is only one window of length 1, so the maximum average is 5.

content.problemStatement:
You receive an integer array `nums` consisting of `n` elements, and an integer `k`.

Identify a contiguous subarray whose **length is equal to** `k` that has the largest average value and output *this value*. Any answer with a calculation error less than `10^-5` will be accepted.

**Example 1:**

```
Input: nums = [1,12,-5,-6,50,3], k = 4
Output: 12.75000
Explanation: Maximum average is (12 - 5 - 6 + 50) / 4 = 51 / 4 = 12.75
```

**Example 2:**

```
Input: nums = [5], k = 1
Output: 5.00000
```

**Constraints:**

* `n == nums.length`
* `1 <= k <= n <= 10^5`
* `-10^4 <= nums[i] <= 10^4`

notes: Comparing window sums avoids repeated summation of the same elements.
The initial window must be used to initialize the maximum, which is important when all valid averages are negative.
solution.approach: Use a sliding window of exactly k elements. Compute the first window sum, then move the window one position at a time by adding the new element and removing the element that leaves the window. Track the largest window sum and divide it by k at the end.

better.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
better.description: Reuse the previous window sum: when the window moves right, add the incoming element and subtract the outgoing element. This reduces each window update to constant time.

optimal.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.
optimal.description: Initialize the sum of the first k elements and use a fixed-size sliding window for the remaining positions. Track the maximum window sum, then divide it by k. Initializing from the first window rather than zero correctly handles arrays whose best average is negative.

bruteForce.complexity: O(n * k) time and O(1) extra space.
bruteForce.description: Compute the sum of every contiguous subarray of length k by summing its k elements directly, then keep the largest average.

followUps: Why is it enough to compare window sums instead of averages?
How would the method change if the window length could vary between two bounds?
Why should the maximum sum be initialized from the first window when negative values are allowed?
